details:
tl;dr: Please let us curate a personal blacklist for world parameters that proactively stops certain worlds from showing up in the discover tab. Ideally granular so we can chose to screen things at the Name, Description or Tag level. 

You could even go one step further and allow us to blacklist upload dates, creator names, dowload sizes, etc.

Longer reasoning below:

As VRChat has grown in size over the years, it has become increasingly hard to discover new and interesting worlds. 

Whenever you look in the Random category in particular (which should be one of the de-facto best ways to explore the game's grand archive of worlds), for every one world worth visting, there are about thirty worlds that fall under what I like to call "worldslop". 

These are visually and thematically very similar worlds that are either "somebody's room" or "a chill hub to sleep and hangout/drink/party in". Often either barely edited prefabs or just profoundly unispired amalgamations of whatever is "popular".

On their own, there is nothing really THAT wrong with these worlds. Because everyone has to start somewhere after all.

But, what this does is create a knock-on-effect where as time goes by it only becomes harder to discover the things made by more skilled and/or creative people. You increasingly need to rely on word-of-mouth or following external platforms for curation, which leads to the general populace being funneled into the same handful of popular maps that siphon activity from the rest of the game.

As an example, if you could completely prevent any worlds from showing up in the Random/New/Community Labs tab that had these in their name, tags or even descriptions:

- Chill

- Sleep

- Relax

- Cozy

- Lounge

- Club

- World

- Home or House

- Apartment

- Hangout

- Room

...the variety of worlds you would come across would shoot up by orders of magnitude. 

I would even go so far as to suggest that one or two of these words should be blacklisted by default - but that's just because of the sheer fatigue I have for these types of worlds after playing this game for almost half a decade. Others may feel less strongly about it than me.

This is also broadly applicable to other use cases as well. Such as people screening for phobias (spiders, snakes, etc.) or just things that don't align with their interests/values (furry, religion, etc.)

Tags alone are also not the solution because of the thousands of legacy worlds floating out there in the digital void that are not tagged properly and never will be tagged properly.
title: Customizable Blacklist for key world parameters in Discover tab
